C. J. Cutcliffe Hyne, The Lost Continent.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/c-j-cutcliffe-hyne/the-lost-continent

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- C. J. Cutcliffe Hyne, the author, died 1944.

First publication of the text used: 1899 in serial form in Pearson's Magazine (United Kingdom), July to December 1899; the book editions of 1900 (SE colophon: 'was published in 1900 by C. J. Cutcliffe Hyne') were issued by Hutchinson (London) and Harper (New York). Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Lost_Continent:_The_Story_of_Atlantis) gives both facts.

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1899, before 1923, so it is in the United States public domain.
- Country of origin (United Kingdom; the serial in Pearson's Magazine came first): copyright there lasts for life plus 70 years after the death of the last person named above. The last to die did so in 1944, so the work entered the public domain there on 1 January 2015.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."
